A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VICON research and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v4 reports original fluid-dynamics prediction experiments, architectural ablations, robustness analyses, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v5 retains these empirical results and adds specialist U-Net, CNN-ICON, cross-trajectory context, and smaller-patch experiments.

M1.justification: The proposed VICON architecture, positional encodings, attention mask, normalization, and rollout Algorithms 1–5 remain unchanged. Shared-projection and normalized-loss explanations add documentation. CNN-ICON is introduced as an experimental architectural comparator, rather than replacing VICON.

E1.justification: The same three fluid datasets and forward-prediction tasks are retained. Sections 5.7 and D.3 add a test scenario using context from other trajectories governed by the same operator, extending the available-input conditions beyond context from the current trajectory.

E2.justification: v5 substantially broadens comparisons by adding individually trained Specialist U-Net-Mod64 models to Table 1 and a whole-frame CNN-ICON comparator in Appendix D.1, Table 10. These introduce specialist forecasting and alternative in-context representation comparisons alongside the retained DPOT, MPP, and non-in-context ViT baselines.

E3.justification: Primary splits, metrics, and training settings remain unchanged. Added experiments introduce 50/50 intra-/cross-trajectory training, CNN-ICON comparison settings, and a reduced 4×4-patch model on an 80GB A100. The reported 8×8-patch token/feedforward widths change from 512/1024 to 256/512; this establishes a reported setting revision without proving that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v5 adds substantial tests of central design choices: whole-frame CNN compression versus patch representations, and intra- versus cross-trajectory context during training and inference. Appendix D.1 also extends the patch-resolution analysis to 4×4 patches and revises Figure 4(a–c). Existing positional-encoding, context-length, missing-frame, turbulence, and joint-training analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version provides benchmark seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. Channelwise standard deviations remain normalization quantities or descriptive field statistics, rather than uncertainty estimates across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Retained VICON/DPOT/MPP results are unchanged, but new specialist results materially expand the comparative findings. Table 1 reports U-Net last-step errors of 48.8, 55.9, and 39.9 on the 1e-2 scale for Incomp, LowVis, and HighVis, respectively, beating joint VICON on Incomp and HighVis. v5 also adds CNN-ICON and cross-trajectory results and revised patch-ablation curves. Table 2's new stride-2 VICON entries repeat values identified elsewhere with stride 3, leaving their setting ambiguous.

T1.justification: The temporally homogeneous Markovian setup and mathematical substance of Equations 1–13 are retained. Explicit mean and standard-deviation expressions explain existing normalization; no new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction adds an explicit qualification that the current implementation addresses passive, autonomous PDEs, leaving non-autonomous externally forced systems for future work. The central contributions and headline accuracy, efficiency, and robustness claims in the abstract and conclusion remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v5 adds explanations connecting shared projections to latent consistency and CNN-ICON's poorer results to lost spatial information. It discusses specialist-versus-multiphysics tradeoffs and explains the database and operator-retrieval requirements of cross-trajectory context. Existing checkerboard, dimensional-scaling, and rollout-error limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v5 explicitly states that training MSE uses normalized values and documents the added U-Net normalization, CNN encoder/decoder, context-sampling mixture, and small-patch hardware and timings. Core configuration tables and code-access information remain unchanged. The CNN comparison's claimed matched six-layer, width-512 configuration is not reconciled with Table 4's ten-layer, width-1024 VICON.

R1.justification: The same cited works are retained; author-year citations and added bibliographic URLs are formatting changes. The new specialist discussion expands VICON's positioning relative to the already-cited PDEArena U-Net, while Appendix D.3 explicitly relates cross-trajectory sampling to the original ICON framework.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. v5 adds focused subsections for specialist implementation and context sampling, expands several explanations, and makes local language corrections. Author information, publication headers, and citation style are updated.

P2.justification: The TMLR conversion substantially changes the title/author block, typography, headers, table-caption placement, and distribution of figures and tables. Table 1 gains a specialist column, Table 2 gains VICON rows and parameter sizes, and new Tables 10 and 12 present added experiments. Figure 4(a–c) has revised curves, axes, and legends; the other figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: v5 improves empirical scrutiny through specialist comparisons that expose performance limits, additional architectural and context-sampling tests, and clearer implementation details. These gains are limited by reporting inconsistencies: Table 2's stride-2 entries repeat reported stride-3 values, the CNN matching configuration is unreconciled with Table 4, and Section 5.1 retains a broad superiority statement despite U-Net winning two datasets. The added evidence supports a modest overall improvement.
